messages:
amy (eng-runtime): heads-up — starting ~1854319800 we saw p99 in us-west jump from ~220ms to ~1.2s when routing spilled some requests to eu-west. quick look shows kernel selection changed and KV-cache misses spiked. dumping traces below.

chao (perf): can you paste the flame/trace and current microbatch size? p95 still okay?

amy (eng-runtime): p95 steady (~280ms). microbatch configured = 4. trace snippet:```
[trace]
0.000 dispatch_request -> select_kernel (selected=int8_fallback)
0.012 kv_cache_lookup miss (prefix_id=abc123)
0.045 schedule_kernel_exec (queue_delay=6ms)
0.180 kernel_exec int8_fallback latency=180ms
0.310 kv_restore replay_tokens=1024 add_latency=520ms
0.830 response_send total_path=830ms (tail case)
```

chao (perf): kv_restore replay_tokens=1024 — that smells like a cache-key mismatch. are we switching model variants between regions (quantized vs fp16)?

matt (infra): @amy which routing policy triggered the cross-region? did us-west lose capacity or was this overflow policy? also add the per-core util/profile output.

amy (eng-runtime): routing policy = spillover_by_region with fallback variant = model-v2-quantized. us-west pool had a brief capacity GC & GPU reclaim (cpu steal ~30%) at spill time. curl snippet I ran: `curl -s "https://console/routing/trace?req=1854321000" | jq .`

ryan (oncall): suggestion: for requests that will be routed cross-region we should reduce microbatching (1-2) to avoid amplifying KV miss replays. cross-region latency + large microbatches = compounding tail. :eyes:

chao (perf): +1. also consider forcing kernel-family affinity for compatible variants so KV keys/serialization stay aligned. kernel mismatch -> different KV layout -> full replay. that explains p95 ok but p99 blowup for long contexts.

amy (eng-runtime): confirmed — model-v2-quantized uses slightly different KV key encoding. when a request spans a route switch we currently accept mismatch and replay, which is cheap at p50 but kills p99 on long-seq requests.

matt (infra): ops note: routing decision latency and cross-region queueing jitter added ~40-60ms median, but the big hit is the replay work. we should push a guardrail in the router: no variant switch unless KV-compat=true or seq_len < 512.

chao (perf): quick simulation plan: run replay-heavy workload with microbatch=[1,2,4] and variants=[same-kernel, quantized-swapped], measure p95/p99 and replay count. I can run overnight.

amy (eng-runtime): creating an incident/epic to track mitigations. short term fixes: (1) route-level microbatch cap for fallback routes = 2, (2) disable variant switching for pinned models, (3) add a fast KV-compat check in select_kernel. long term: adaptive microbatcher that lowers batch size when route != primary.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026 created (eng-runtime) — assigned to amy, chao, matt.

ryan (oncall): sounds good. if you want I can push a temporary routing flag to prefer same-variant instances for tail-critical routes.

amy (eng-runtime): will run the sim tonight and post perf numbers. TL;DR: root cause = combination of (a) kernel selection mismatch across variants -> KV encoding mismatch, (b) microbatch sizing that magnified replay cost, (c) cross-region queueing jitter. short-term guardrails listed above. cc @chao @matt :thumbsup:
